{"decision":"RECORDED AS A MEASURED DEFECT PLUS AN OPEN QUESTION. Found 2026-08-05 by the FIRST REAL TRIAL of cap:corpus-ingest, over six architecture documents from dev_storyflow. Nothing here is settled, and the fix shape is genuinely open.

⭐ THE MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS THE WHOLE FINDING. `dynograph_resolution::token_sort_ratio`, which `ingest::fuzzy_match` uses on node NAMES, against the auto-merge threshold of 90:

  95  dynograph-vector   vs dynograph-core        <- SILENTLY MERGED
  94  dynograph-storage  vs dynograph-core        <- SILENTLY MERGED
  93  dynograph-extract  vs dynograph-context     <- SILENTLY MERGED
  91  dynograph-server   vs dynograph-query       <- SILENTLY MERGED
  89  dynograph-engine   vs dynograph-core        (asked)
  84  Auth Service       vs Authentication Service (NOT merged, NOT asked at Component's 90/80 bands)

THE THRESHOLD IS EXACTLY BACKWARDS FOR THE NAMES REAL SYSTEMS USE. Sibling modules sharing a prefix — the near-universal convention — score 91-95 and are merged without asking. The canonical duplicate the feature exists to catch, `Auth Service` ~ `Authentication Service`, scores 84 and is not. `docs/scope-corpus-ingest.md` asserted "90 on a token-sorted ratio is near-identity"; MEASURED, IT IS NOT.

THE IMPACT, MEASURED ON ONE DOCUMENT: dynograph.md declares NINE crates. After ingest the graph holds FIVE. FOUR CRATES — 44% of the architecture — WERE SILENTLY DESTROYED (dynograph-core, dynograph-vector, dynograph-query, dynograph-extract are gone as named nodes). And the survivors ASSERT SOMETHING FALSE rather than merely being incomplete: `cmp:dynograph-core` now carries the name "dynograph-storage", because the merged node keeps the first id and the longer name. The longer-name rule is BL-186's own #73 fix working exactly as designed — the defect is the merge, not the naming.

⭐ THIS IS NOT A CORPUS DEFECT AND THE TRIAL NEARLY MISDIAGNOSED IT. The first reading blamed the new corpus driver. Isolating dynograph.md and ingesting it ALONE reproduces it exactly: 9 in, 5 out, 4 merges. So this is PRE-EXISTING IN `ingest` and has been true of every single-document ingest since fuzzy dedup landed. The corpus layer is only the first thing to put enough same-family names in front of it for the loss to be visible. Everything this project has ingested one document at a time may carry it.

WHY NOBODY SAW IT: reflow2's own design uses prose names ("The graph handle is an accepted single point of failure"), not prefixed identifier names. `dev_storyflow` is a CODEBASE, so its architecture documents are full of `foo-bar` sibling crates. Self-host was structurally incapable of surfacing this — the same shape as BL-199, and the second time that shape has explained a long-invisible defect.

DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS `dec:ask-not-repair` IN PRACTICE WHILE OBEYING IT IN FORM. The ruling says suspected duplicates are asked, never silently merged; the 90+ band is treated as "not a suspicion" and acts. The measurement says the 90+ band CONTAINS the very cases most in need of asking, so the rule is honoured and its purpose defeated.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) RAISE THE AUTO-MERGE THRESHOLD. Cheap, and wrong on its own: 95 was a sibling pair, so there is no threshold that separates them by score. (b) NEVER AUTO-MERGE — every match becomes a question, and the corpus batching (BL-186) is what makes that affordable. Honest and expensive; the 11-candidate band in the same trial was 11/11 FALSE POSITIVES, so a user would be answering "no" a great many times. (c) A DISCRIMINATOR BEYOND THE SCORE — refuse to merge when the names differ by a whole token that neither contains ("core" vs "storage" are not variants of each other, while "Auth" vs "Authentication" is a prefix). This targets the actual failure and is the option worth designing. (d) EMBEDDINGS as the tiebreaker in the band, which `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` already asks about — and this trial is the strongest evidence yet FOR it, because the lexical signal is not merely weak here, it is INVERTED. (e) MAKE IT LOUD RATHER THAN CORRECT — keep merging but report every merge for review. Weakest alone, necessary in any case.

MY OWN DEFECT, FOUND BY THE SAME TRIAL AND FIXED BY NOBODY YET: `CorpusReport.fuzzy_merges` is a `usize`. The single-document `IngestReport` carries `Vec<FuzzyMerge>` and its doc comment says "auditable, never silent" — the corpus aggregate reduces that to a COUNT, so at exactly the scale where silent merges matter most, WHAT was merged is unrecoverable from the report. That is a regression I introduced in BL-186 and it should be fixed before anyone runs a real corpus.

NOT MEASURED, AND IT BOUNDS EVERYTHING ABOVE: what this does to the other 1,118 documents. The trial was SIX documents chosen for topical overlap. The 44% figure is one document's crate list, not a corpus-wide rate.","name":"OPEN — auto-merge at 90 silently destroys SIBLING components and misses the duplicates it exists to catch; the threshold is backwards for real naming conventions","rationale":"Filed the moment the trial produced it, with the scores rather than the impression, because "fuzzy matching is too aggressive" is the kind of claim that decays into folklore and then gets re-argued from scratch. The six numbers are reproducible from `dynograph_resolution::token_sort_ratio` directly.

Recorded as its own node rather than as an amendment to `cap:corpus-ingest` because the capability is not where the defect lives — isolating a single document proved it is `ingest`'s, and attaching it to the corpus capability would have embalmed the misdiagnosis the trial itself corrected.

The self-criticism about `CorpusReport.fuzzy_merges` is on the node deliberately: the trial's most useful property was that it could show WHAT converged, and the shipped report cannot. Recording that where the fix will be read is worth more than recording it where it would be flattering.","status":"proposed"}
